solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A song givin' clue to Tina?

parts.note: read the title as wordplay: four letters behaving badly, rearranged, spell the name Tina

explanation.surface: A setter offers a tune as a hint for someone called Tina.
explanation.walkthrough: The title read cryptically says AINT is mixed up, and AINT rearranged gives TINA, so the song title is itself the clue to Tina.
explanation.definitionFit: Fats Waller's jazz standard of 1929 is a famous song with this title.

clue.text: Metal, mostly nickel, extracted centrally in plant

indicators.note: mostly means the metal's name loses its final letter

parts.note: zinc is a metallic element
Ni is the chemical symbol for nickel

indicators.note: centrally means only the middle letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: A plant has absorbed metal, chiefly nickel, from the soil.
explanation.definitionFit: A zinnia is a brightly coloured garden flower of the daisy family, a type of plant.

clue.text: Say, I am up, taking shower — it's very painful

indicators.note: taking means the first pieces hold the next one inside them
in a down clue, up means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: say is abbreviated e.g., for example
I am contracts to I'm
a shower is a brief fall of rain

explanation.surface: Someone getting up and into the shower complains of a pounding pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say, I am' looks like the start of a sentence, but it gives two abbreviations, turned together by 'up' to make MIGE before 'taking' adds the shower.
explanation.definitionFit: A migraine is a severe recurring headache, notably painful.

clue.text: An official ultimately spins work out, embodying a possible example of this?

definitions.text: An official ultimately spins work out, embodying a possible example of this?

indicators.note: embodying means the jumbled letters take the following word inside them
out signals the preceding letters are rearranged, as in worked out
ultimately means only the last letter of the word official is used

explanation.surface: A bureaucrat drags a task out to fill the time, perhaps illustrating a famous principle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges AN, L and SPINSWORK, and 'embodying' puts A inside; the whole clue also describes the law in action.
explanation.definitionFit: Parkinson's law says work expands to fill the time available, exactly what an official spinning a job out shows.

clue.text: Girl entertaining, for starters — one's found on the outskirts of Hiroshima?

definitions.text: Girl entertaining, for starters — one's found on the outskirts of Hiroshima?

indicators.note: for starters means the opening letters of the two words before it

parts.note: one's read as one is gives I plus S

indicators.note: on the outskirts of means only the first and last letters of the place name

explanation.surface: An entertaining girl, one met at the edge of a Japanese city.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a Japanese girl who entertains, of the kind found around Hiroshima.
explanation.definitionFit: A geisha is a Japanese hostess trained to entertain guests, a girl entertaining in Japan.

clue.text: Lively party providing constant excitement

parts.note: c is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
arousal is a state of excitement

explanation.surface: A party with non-stop thrills.
explanation.definitionFit: A carousal is a noisy drinking spree, a rowdy party.

clue.text: Dodgy claim put on home insurance initially is opposed

indicators.note: put on means in an across clue the first piece comes after the next

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter of insurance is used
dodgy suggests the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: An insurer resists a suspicious home insurance claim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dodgy' rearranges the claim into MICAL; in an across clue 'put on' places that after the home and insurance letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Inimical means hostile or unfriendly, set against something.

clue.text: Artist's a Turner Prize

indicators.note: a turner turns things round, so the artist's word is read backwards

parts.note: an artist who draws is a drawer

explanation.surface: An artist wins the Turner Prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a Turner' turns DRAWER round. The Turner Prize is a famous British art award, so 'Turner Prize' reads as one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A reward is a prize given for an achievement.

clue.text: Letter concerning endless gossip after doctor left last practice

indicators.note: after says the pieces before it follow the doctor in the answer

parts.note: ess is the spelt-out name of the letter S
re means concerning, about

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: hearsay is rumour or gossip

explanation.surface: A doctor walked out after a letter about rumours before a final session.
explanation.definitionFit: A dress rehearsal is the final full run-through before a performance.

clue.text: Book suggesting passion fruit?

parts.note: passion is wrath, and fruit is grapes, so a title naming grapes of anger fits

explanation.surface: A novel that hints at a tropical fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Passion fruit is a real fruit; here 'passion' is anger and 'fruit' is a bunch of grapes, giving Steinbeck's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Steinbeck's 1939 novel bears this title, so it is a book.

clue.text: Vocal part essential to Britten oratorio

indicators.note: essential to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A singing part that is central to a Britten choral work.
explanation.definitionFit: The tenor is the high adult male voice part in choral music.

clue.text: Soundly checks colour of edging for flags?

indicators.note: soundly says the words are said aloud to give the spelling

parts.note: checks are curbs, and colour is tone, so curb's tone

explanation.surface: A thorough inspection of the colour of bunting.
explanation.walkthrough: Flags here are flagstones of a pavement; a British kerb is the US curb, the edge of the pavement.
explanation.definitionFit: Kerbstones form the raised edge of a pavement made of flagstones.

clue.text: One's potentially a Latin

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: potentially suggests the letters could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: Someone might be of Latin stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potentially' turns A LATIN into TALIAN after I; the whole clue also defines, since an Italian is a Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: Italians are a Latin people, descended from the speakers of Latin.

clue.text: Exalts, putting positive first?

parts.note: exalts can mean raises, and putting the P for positive in front gives another word for exalts

explanation.surface: Someone lauds others, always looking on the bright side.
explanation.walkthrough: RAISES means exalts; put P (positive) first and the new word also means exalts.
explanation.definitionFit: To praise is to extol or glorify, the same as exalting.

clue.text: Is in favour of France finally withdrawing after hurtful comment by Le Figaro

indicators.note: after says the following pieces come behind the hurtful comment
by means the article is placed beside the rest

parts.note: a barb is a cutting remark

indicators.note: withdrawing means these pieces go backwards

parts.note: is means lives, exists
for means in favour of

indicators.note: finally means only the last letter of France is used

parts.note: le is taken as written

explanation.surface: A French newspaper prints a cutting jibe about someone backing out of France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdrawing' turns LIVES, FOR and E into EROFSEVIL. 'Le Figaro' is a French newspaper; Figaro is the barber in Rossini's opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Figaro is the title character of Rossini's opera, the barber of the Spanish city.

clue.text: Vanessa Redgrave's editor?

definitions.meaning: a left-wing actress, so a red performer
one who prepares text for publication

explanation.definitionFit: A redactor is one who edits text, and Redgrave is a famously left-wing actress.

clue.text: Take, perhaps, a long time eating one waffle

parts.note: take is an example of a verb
one is the Roman numeral I
an age is a long time

explanation.surface: Someone takes ages over a breakfast waffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Waffle is wordy empty talk, which is verbiage.

clue.text: Conceal building without walls that's awful to look at

parts.note: to hide is to conceal

indicators.note: without walls means the outer letters of the building are removed

parts.note: a house is a building

explanation.surface: Hiding an ugly building without walls.
explanation.definitionFit: Hideous means very ugly, horrible to see.

clue.text: Youngster loses pound under yellow flower

indicators.note: under in a down clue puts the first-named piece below the colour

parts.note: or is gold or yellow in heraldry

indicators.note: loses means a letter is removed from the word

parts.note: a child is a youngster

explanation.surface: A child drops some money under a yellow bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses' takes L from CHILD to leave CHID. OR is the heraldic name for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchid is an exotic flowering plant.

clue.text: It must be good for one to make it

definitions.text: It must be good for one to make it

parts.words: It must be good for one to make it
parts.note: making a lot of money and having good luck are both senses: you make one, and good one is luck

explanation.surface: Something must be worthwhile for someone to bother producing it.
explanation.walkthrough: Good fortune is luck, and one 'makes a fortune' by getting rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Fortune is wealth or luck; you make a fortune and have good fortune.

clue.text: Relative coming up short's regularly laid bare

indicators.note: coming up short means the word falls short of its last letter

parts.note: an uncle is a relative

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of laid

explanation.surface: A relative falling short is regularly exposed.
explanation.definitionFit: Unclad means unclothed, naked.

clue.text: Second in charge is caught in corruption shock

indicators.note: in means the letter is placed inside the run of the other words

parts.note: vice is corruption, wickedness
a shock of hair
c is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A deputy is caught up in a corruption scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: A vice-chair is the deputy of a committee chair.

clue.text: I, with heart of venom, want villain to suffer

indicators.note: heart of means the middle letter of venom

parts.note: a cur is a contemptible man, a scoundrel

explanation.surface: Someone venomously wants a villain punished.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur a loss is to suffer or bring it on oneself.

clue.text: Drama's satisfactory and that is it

parts.note: Noh, also spelt No, is a Japanese drama
OK means satisfactory

explanation.surface: A play that is good enough and nothing more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' here is the slang for sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Nookie is slang for sex, also called it.

clue.text: Marks and Spencer's first backed it at AGM, for a change

indicators.note: first means just the opening letter of Spencer
backed means the word is reversed
for a change says the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Marks and Spencer's shareholders support a change at the annual meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marks and Spencer' is a British retail chain. 'backed' turns IT into TI; 'for a change' rearranges ATAGM to GMATA.
explanation.definitionFit: Stigmata are marks, especially the wounds of Christ.
